===Levels 55–99: Knights of Ardougne===
[[File:Theoretical max xp ardy knight.png|thumb|Using different items, or completing the medium [[Ardougne Diary]] tasks will change experience rates.]]
Pickpocketing [[Knight of Ardougne|Knights of Ardougne]] is a slower but more straightforward alternative to the faster training methods. A knight can be lured so that the player can continuously pickpocket them without moving the mouse. The player will occasionally need to open the [[coin pouch]]es to continue pickpocketing.

Completing the [[Ardougne Diary#Medium|medium Ardougne Diary]] is strongly recommended for a 10% higher success rate of pickpocketing. Use [[dodgy necklace]]s to have a 25% chance to resist being stunned and taking damage, which increases experience rates slightly. Wearing full [[rogue equipment]] grants double loot per pickpocket, though no extra experience is given. With completion of [[A Kingdom Divided]], [[Shadow Veil]] can be used for an extra chance to resist the stun, stacking with dodgy necklaces for a total of 36.25%, though shadow veil starts to lose value around level 90. If using shadow veil, players should bring a lava staff and a stack of cosmic runes.  

The experience rates in the table below assume the player has completed the medium Ardougne Diary and is using dodgy necklaces. The rates also assume some time is spent on mistakes and opening the coin pouches. Players stop failing to pickpocket Knights of Ardougne at level 95 with the medium diary perk, from which point onwards the tick-perfect rate is 252,900 experience per hour.

Training from level 55 to level 99 on Knights of Ardougne would yield around {{Coins|7,630,000}} without rogue equipment, and roughly {{Coins|15,260,000}} with the full set. Players can expect to use roughly 200 dodgy necklaces and need to heal 16,000 hitpoints worth of damage (with natural regeneration taken into account at 1x hitpoints restore rate) from level 55 to 95.

====Lure north of the market====
[[File:Ardougne Knight trap.png|thumb|left|An example of a trapped knight, with highlighted which tile to start shoving from, as well as a knight in the resulting trap.]]
Attack the knight located in the south-eastern part of the Ardougne marketplace. Specifically the knight that re spawns 5 tiles west of the Ardougne agility course starting point. Lure her towards the building to the north of the marketplace. Stand in the doorway of that building so that the knight is standing on the tile south of the player. Run two squares west so the knight should stand one tile east of the player. Then run into the square south of the doorway so the knight will stand on the doorway. Use the [[dragon spear]]'s [[special attack]]s on the knight, and quickly run inside and close the door before the knight is able to walk back outside. If the player does not have a dragon spear, it is possible to walk under the knight to force it to walk backwards but it may take a few attempts for it to walk the right direction. After waiting a while, the knight will move to the southern most two tiles of the house. She will only be able to move between those two tiles. If she is able to move elsewhere, the wrong knight has been lured.

Players can also simply hop worlds until they find one where the knight has already been lured.

After the knight has been lured correctly, stand north of her. Turn your camera to face west, lower it all the way down, and zoom in. This way you are able to spam-click the same spot (around the chest) to pickpocket. It is important to not stand on either of the two tiles she is able to walk on, as she will stop moving causing her to despawn after 5 minutes of stationary activity.

====Splashing====
Another option is to use a [[splashing]] [[Account#Alternative accounts|account]] to keep a knight into place. This can be done anywhere if the splashing account simply tanks the knight, but this requires having high Defence and wearing good defensive armour along with the [[Hitpoints cape]] and [[regen bracelet]]. Alternatively, lure a knight to a spot where the splasher is able to safespot the knight, such as in the south-eastern bank of Ardougne where it is possible to use the fences as blockades. The knight will not despawn as long as he is aggressive towards the splasher, and the splashing account stays logged in if it is attacking or tanking the knight. Splashing is performed on "sticky knights," a term to describe a knight that moves a lot less as it has been forced out of its natural wander range. This will always be a female knight for the south bank.

Players can also bring a stack of law runes and a staff giving unlimited water runes instead of food to make the process more simple. After death two law runes and the staff will be kept, enabling the player to quickly teleport back to the Ardougne marketplace. Pick up your coins and stack of law runes off the ground and continue pickpocketing. Enabling [[Rapid Heal]] can help extend trips longer.

Players can often find someone splashing a knight in the south bank on the following worlds, with many players taking part in pickpocketing the targeted knight.

====Zero mouse movement strategy====
Position the coin pouches over the knight and then open the inventory with the assigned F‑key, click on the coin pouches to open them, and then close the inventory again with the F‑key. This drastically reduces the mouse movement required for pickpocketing.

Moving the inventory can be done by using Resizable – Classic layout or the Resizable – Modern layout and moving the inventory by holding Alt and dragging it over the Knight with your mouse. This can also be achieved by adjusting the inventory position through a combination of window resizing, camera zoom, and camera angle.

This strategy also works for the Shadow Veil spell by using the Filters option in your spellbook. Unselect all the spell filters except for Show Utility spells. Then use the F-key assigned to the spellbook to open it, click on shadow veil to activate it, and finally close the spellbook again by using the assigned F-key.
